title: Content-Security-Policy script-src allows data: scripts
description: The script-src directive lists the data: scheme as an allowed source. A data: script executes in the document's context even though its URL has an opaque origin, so an attacker who can inject markup or a URL can supply script bytes without hosting a file on any allowed origin. The check reports the scheme source; it does not claim an injection point exists.
remediation: Remove data: from script-src (and from default-src when script-src is absent) and serve scripts from a fixed HTTPS origin, preferably with a nonce or hash.
limitation: Observation-level: reads script-src only. A policy that allows data: through default-src without a script-src override is a separate scope and is not reported by this check.
scopeT: One response: script-src contains a data: scheme source.
fp: An application that deliberately ships scripts as data: URLs is reported by design; the pattern is rare and weakens the origin boundary.
recordDesc: A policy allows data: scripts. Data URLs carry their bytes in the URL, so a script can be assembled from text that never touches an allowed script origin. Browsers execute it in the page context, which defeats the origin restriction the policy intends to enforce.
applicability: HTTPS applications that set Content-Security-Policy with script-src or inherit it from default-src.
risk: Script execution from a scheme with no host origin; MEDIUM severity.
why: The script-src source list contains the data: scheme.
fix: Serve scripts from a fixed HTTPS origin with a nonce or hash.
verifyT: Parse the policy and confirm neither script-src nor an inherited default-src contains data:.

cells.safe: script-src restricted to HTTPS origins and a nonce
